questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
That subjects were taught in English and the city had a prominent and vibrant cultural life.
Also, that the weather was somewhat hot (Spoiler alert: I didn't do my research proporly).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Exchange has been such a fun experience! Melbourne is a fantastic city and very easy to live in. I have left the city with friends for life and a minor vape addiction.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Everything's in English. Signs are English. Tramp voices are in English. People are English. Amazing how all information is available in English ey?

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance. I guess the University offers some if you need it tho, they are used to babysit american exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It is NOT easy. There's a rental crisis in Australia. I found a share house through a friend who lives in Melbs. 
I recommend the Facebook group 'Fairy Floss' to find accommodation. I'll warn you, there's a lot of people trying to get a roof over their head and it furthers the challenge that you are not located in Australia. It is not impossible, you just have to text a thousand people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I found living off campus the ideal choice for me. Lived with four cute Aussie girlies in a suburb. Biking distance to uni and great public transport if you're into that sort of thing. If you live in student accommodation provided by the university you'll be living in shared apartments with other exchange students in the CBD – which I know people also found very fun!
Personally I loved living with Aussies who could teach me about all the treasures in Melbs.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It sucks. I could not afford the university accommodation even if I wanted to. It's insanely expensive. And finding housing off campus is quite a task. I found housing 5 days before departing and stayed at a hostel for a few days before moving into my share house. (btw a lot of people start in hostels which is a nice opportunity to meet other travellers or people on working holiday who shares the accommodation stress).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I can't really remember much from registration – which probably means it was easy?
I remember it was time-consuming finding documents, applying for visa, finding accommodation, renting out my own place, applying for subjects yada yada yada. There wasn't much help to find but I succeeded somehow without any bigger issues.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The university writes e-mails every time you need to provide some information. Which ended up being a lot.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: idk. I couldn't find any. I just hoped for the best – and you know what? it turned out completely fine.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Went great! Got all of them and it was even possible to change subjects up to 2 weeks into the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I know it's frustrating and time-consuming with all the paper work before departing. BUT it's worth it and just like me you'll forget about it pretty quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nice! Fun subjects, charismatic lecturers, creative expression and all in all a great academic programme! It's a long time since I have had this much fun in school!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: New brain level achieved! Or, idk, I learned a lot and had fun while doing it! My subjects weren't the most academic or reading heavy and teachers were very helpfull and enjoyed their field.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were almost no reading. A lot of the subjects allowed for creative expression and hands on experience. The assignments are posted in the beginning of the semester so you can plan out everything and start early. The exams are also shorter word-wise than I'm used to in UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Chinese Music Ensamble, Light in performance, The Art of Game Music & The Business of Music, .

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Uff haha, all of them! Bear in mind that some of the subjects are taught online – meaning you will never meet your teacher or any students who also follows the class. It can be a bit lonesome and might not be the experience you are looking for going on exchange. I had one class on parkville campus and one on southbank and then two online. Loved all of them, and happy I got to experience both city campuses.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
The house I was living in had a few things that needed to be fixed. I think it was a total of 400$. 
Then there's also the cost of visa, insurance and your own travel insurance(thanks for paying my travel insurance mom). Plane tickets are expensive too. And if you want to travel Aussie while you're here – you've guessed it – expensive.  
And you need to quit smoking since a pack of ciggies are 50$. You might think that vaping is cheaper, but you'll soon find yourself vaping on your couch, in your bed and while cooking breakfast – that cost also quickly adds up. Don't smoke kids.
what else, what else, what else...... ohh yeah shows! concerts, comedy, footy, festivals – the temptations are all around you!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Pricing is just like in Denmark even more expensive in some areas – this includes everything related to "fun" like grocery shopping, getting beers, gym memberships, nightlife and taking your cat to the vet. Some people will try and convince you it's cheap going out for dinner – they be lying. Bikes are cheap! but everybody hates cyclists and will try to end your life on a daily basis – especially in the CBD.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of uni clubs you can join and make friends. I joined the Mountaineering club, but only attended one event since spots were limited and the demand were high. Some clubs are more popular than others and slow idiots like me don't stand a chance to get into the surfing club.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sooo so so many. They will let you know at orientation.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
There's so much happening at campus, find something that suits you!
I didn't join any uni clubs, but joined a few bouldering gyms and also had a friend who I biked around Victoria with. There's such amazing nature all around Melbourne, jump on a train and go explore.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get a bike! I loved mine, they are cheap on Facebook marketplace or you can find one at the bike shed – which is a fun community located in Brunswick.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Extremely easy. Almost wished I would have gotten a bigger culture shock. 
Oh one thing! I got stood up by four different dudes who invited me out on a date – I mean the AUDACITY!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Uff tough one. People are busy with their life – just like in Cph. Most people are very friendly and can easily be chat up in class and convinced to go for a beer after class. Or you can join a club!  I was fortunate to live with locals, so they took me to events where I met other Aussies. But I would say that your best odds are to socialize with other exchange students since they're as eager to make new friends as you are!
I would also recommend dating (haha even though you might get stood up). I made a lot of friends on dating apps and went for some super cute dates around the city.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Aussie slang. You will begin to speak English in another way – a more fun way.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are super chill and are very friendly! Coffee and craft beer is on point. There's a thousand things going on around the city and they have lovely parks everywhere!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have fun! Uni Melb and Melbourne in general provides so many opportunities it can be overwhelming. Find your own way in your exchange. Enjoy the beautiful hogwards like campus and explore the city and the great nature Victoria has to offer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nahh you'll be fine.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Awww difficult question – I appreciate everything and already miss it!
Enjoy the excellent classes and the wonderful people while you can<3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Exam period. You can stay on top of the game by starting your exam writing early. I didn't. It's just my nature. So I was batteling deadlines at the end while getting ready to move out and saying goodbye to people. Don't be like me. Be better.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you are debating going on exchange, I hope after reading this you aren't anymore. If you want to do it, you just got to do it! For me it was worth every worry, every second, every cent!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
